note: Triennial election of the rural district council, polled 31 May 1911. Filed from the nomination list (Armagh Guardian, 28 April 1911, p. 2), the withdrawals (Armagh Guardian, 5 May 1911, p. 3) and the results of the contests in Ballyards, Clady, Grange, Lisnadill and Middletown (Armagh Guardian, 2 June 1911, p. 3). Not filed: Armagh Rural (6 nominated) and Tynan (3), whose withdrawals were not found, and Crossmore, where W. Menary withdrew leaving a contest between A. Gordon (U.), R. Watson (U.) and Peter Mooney (N.) whose result was not found. Labels are printed only for the Armagh Rural and Clady nominees and in some results. Returned unopposed. T. A. M'Clure: no party label printed in 1911. At other elections he stood as Unionist (Glenaul, 25 May 1905, printed 'U': Armagh Guardian, 2 June 1905, p. 5 (Armagh rural district council results, counted by Mr. Calvert); nominations from the Armagh Guardian, 28 April 1905, p. 5 ("Guardians' Nominations"; "All the candidates are Unionists save where marked N.") and Armagh Guardian, 5 May 1905, p. 4 ("Poor Law Guardians": contests and withdrawals); Glenaul, 28 May 1914, printed 'U': Armagh Guardian, 5 June 1914, p. 3 ("Armagh Rural Council"); nominations from the Northern Whig, 9 May 1914, p. 10 ("Rural Councils: Armagh": nominations received 30 April and withdrawals)).
